title: operators-triage-timeline-and-dashboard-matrix
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight working playbook for oncall operators and dashboard owners that maps an investigation timeline to the minimum set of telemetry and traces we need to resolve common LLM inference degradations (latency spikes, cache coldness, model fallback loops). The goal is to reduce mean time to insight by prescribing: 1) a prioritized metric set, 2) trace anchoring rules, and 3) a compact dashboard matrix for each investigation window.

Context and assumptions:
- For tokenized inference, a large fraction of incidents are due to: KV cache misses, batching backpressure, network egress to model backends, or routing fallbacks to cheaper model variants.
- Operators need a 3-stage timeline view: immediate (0-3min), short (3-30min), and deep (30+min).
- We prioritize low-cardinality rollups for immediate triage and sample traces for deep troubleshooting.

Quick glossary (how I use terms in this doc):
- Request latency: end-to-end time between request accepted by front proxy and final token stream completion.
- Token tail latency: 95th/99th token generation delta after first token.
- KV warmth: ratio of requests served with prefix/KV cache hit (by tenant/model).
- Batch fullness: average tokens/request in active batch window.

Prioritized metrics (definitions, primary owner, immediate alert thresholds):
1) edge.request.p50|p95|p99 (ms) - end-to-end request latency buckets
   owner: Lina Zhou
   alert: p99 > 1200ms sustained > 5m
   notes: tagged by route/model/region/tenant. For immediate triage rely on route-level p95+p99 only.

2) kv.cache.hit_ratio (percent) - fraction of requests hitting prefix/KV cache
   owner: Samir Patel
   alert: drop > 30pp from baseline for primary model in a region
   notes: calculate as hits/(hits+misses) sampled at 1s granularity. If low, expand to per-tenant.

3) serving.batch.fill_rate (0-1) - how full batches are when dispatched
   owner: Serving Runtime (oncall)
   alert: fill_rate < 0.25 and request queue length > 50
   notes: low fill_rate + long queue indicates serialization/backpressure.

4) router.fallback.rate (pct) - percent of requests routed off preferred model
   owner: Routing Team
   alert: sustained > 5% increase vs baseline
   notes: correlated with capacity constraints or model OOMs.

5) worker.err.rate (5m) - infra/GPU worker error rate (oom, cuda errors)
   owner: SRE
   alert: any non-zero surge in worker.err.rate tied to model type
   notes: tie with GPU utilization and per-worker logs.

Trace anchoring rules (how to pick traces for different stages):
- Immediate (0-3m): sample 1 trace per route per minute at high severity weight; prefer traces with last-span duration > 500ms. Spans: front-proxy -> router -> runtime -> backend-model.
- Short (3-30m): adaptive sampling: 10% of requests with p99 latency and 1% of p50. Include KV cache span annotations (cache.hit=true/false) and batch-id tag.
- Deep (30+m): retain full traces for 24h for investigations. When replication required, capture additional runtime internal spans (kernel selection, quantization fallback).

Span design recommendations (practical):
- Standardize these span tags: request_id, route, tenant_id (hashed), model, batch_id, cache_hit (bool), seq_len_in, seq_len_out, worker_id
- Add a numeric "token_progress" tag on runtime spans to allow token-level waterfall for long generations.

Dashboard matrix (compact widgets for each investigation window):
Immediate (0-3m) - goal: Isolate whether the problem is client-side, network, routing, or runtime
- Route-level latency heatmap (p95 by route) - dimension: region, tenant top-20
- Global request rate and error rate sparkline - 1m resolution
- Top 5 tenants by p99 - quick suspect list
- Trace-sampler panel: recent sampled traces with short links (one-click open)
- KV hit ratio rolling 5m by model (sparkline)

Short (3-30m) - goal: Find contributing components and correlate signals
- Batch fullness and queue length over time (per-region)
- Router fallback trend and model variant failures (5m)
- Worker GPU utilization vs worker.err.rate scatter panel (5m buckets)
- Span-latency breakdown waterfall (median + p95 overlays) for sampled traces
- Tenant cohort panel: p50/p95/p99 for affected tenants vs baseline cohort

Deep (30+m) - goal: root cause and planned remediation steps
- Long-tail trace gallery with annotations (KV misses, model fallback, OOM)
- Per-worker flamegraphs for internal runtime spans (kernel selection, decode)
- Prefix-level KV heatmap: which prefixes cause misses
- Historical rollout correlation: deploys, config changes, autoscaler events overlay
- Cost impact table: tokens served vs extra latency cost estimate

Widget queries & cheat snippets (examples - adapt to our telemetry backends):
- KV hit ratio (pseudo-SQL):
  SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) AS t, sum(kv_hit)::float / sum(kv_hit+kv_miss) AS hit_ratio FROM inference_kv_events WHERE model = 'rwd-7b' GROUP BY t ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT 60;
- Batch fill rate (promQL style):
  avg_over_time(serving_batch_fill_rate[5m]) by (region)
- Route p99 sparkline (clickable to drill):
  topk(20, quantile_over_time(0.99, edge_request_latency_ms[5m])) by (route)

Investigation play sequence (operator checklist):
Immediate:
- Check route-level p95/p99 and request rate. If route p99 elevated but rate steady, probe traces.
- Look at KV hit ratio; if hit_ratio falls -> label as "cache-cold" and escalate to runtime.
- Check router.fallback.rate; if high, accept degradation and open fallback ticket.

Short:
- Correlate low batch.fill_rate with increased queue length -> throttle tuning or autoscaler changes
- Inspect worker.err.rate + GPU util: if errors spike and utilization high -> possible OOM or bad kernel
- Pull sample traces flagged with cache_hit=false and high token tail -> reproduce with request replay tool (see linked artifacts)

Deep:
- If KV prefix hotspots identified, export top prefixes to solutions-eng for prewarm strategy
- Run per-worker trace flamegraphs and check kernel selection logs for recent driver/patch changes
- Draft rollback or canary adjustments (control plane) and coordinate with release-eng

Runbook: alerts -> required widgets -> escalation matrix
- Auto-alerts should attach the 3 immediate widgets and one sampled trace link. On escalation, pager to runtime oncall and engineer who owns model routing.

Operational notes and heuristics (less formal):
- Low-cardinality first: when in doubt, reduce cardinality (region/route) for immediate pics; expand to tenant only if needed.
- Prefer ratio metrics (hit ratios) over raw counters for triage speed.
- Use hashed tenant ids on dashboards to preserve privacy.
- Keep trace retention parity in case we need to correlate across stages (30d cheap-sampled vs 24h full-sampled).

Dashboard lifecycle and ownership suggestions:
- Each dashboard widget must list: metric owner, query owner, and last-verified date.
- Quarterly audit to prune widgets with >25% query cost per quarter.
- Ownership: assign a primary (oncall rotation) and secondary (dashboard steward).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How quickly can we add cache_hit tag to all runtime spans across older models? (ACTION: Samir -> assess work effort by 2025-03-10)
- Sampling budget: current trace budget is 2000/day; propose to shift 500/day to immediate high-severity bucket. (ACTION: Ava)
- Should we implement an auto-snapshot feature that stores the last 5 full traces on a high-severity alert? (DISCUSS in next triage sync)

Action items (next steps):
- Samir: instrument cache_hit tag for runtime spans on rwd-7b and rwd-13b (due 2025-03-10)
- Lina: create immediate dashboard template (3 widgets) and wire drill links to trace UI (due 2025-03-14)
- Jon: add a promQL view for batch.fill_rate and test alert thresholds on staging (due 2025-03-12)

Notes to self: this doc is intentionally compact — aim for a 1-page quick triage play and a deeper appendix if needed. Keep it lightweight and iterate from real incidents.

References and context links:
- Incident runbook canonical: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/incident-response-playbook
- Trace UI: https://traces.redwood.ai/ (internal)
- Related RFCs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/57
